title: Streak a blood agar plate for single colonies with a flexible loop while holding the lid ajar
instruction: Streak the plate for single colonies, then discard the loop.
context: Streaking a specimen out for isolated colonies is the first physical step of almost every bacterial culture in clinical, food-safety, pharmaceutical and research labs, done many times a day by medical laboratory scientists (O*NET 29-2011) and microbiologists (19-1022). Clinical labs streak each specimen this way before any identification or antibiotic test; their staff are under 500,000, so this is filed as specialised lab work (Other). It goes wrong when a later quadrant drags specimen back from the first, the loop is pressed until it cuts the agar, or the lid is set down or carried off. It is hard because a 2 g plastic loop with a flexible neck must glide with a few grams of force over agar 4 mm deep inside a 15 mm dish, in four ordered zigzags that each start through the previous one, while the other hand holds the lid ajar over the plate. Unlike tasks that flame or carry a loop, or draw a fixed mark, the streak pattern itself is scored.
setup: World metres: x forward from the arm bases, y left, z up; bases (0,+/-0.305,0.750); bench top z=0.7475; every part zero yaw. 1) Plate base (free, 33.3 g): clear polystyrene 90 x 15 mm Petri dish base (EN ISO 24998 size class): outside diameter 88.0 mm, wall 0.8 mm, floor 1.0 mm, height 14.0 mm, outer rim edge rounded 0.4 mm; underside centre at (0.165,0.000,0.7475). It holds 23.2 mL of 5% sheep blood agar, 86.0 mm across and 4.0 mm deep, surface 5.0 mm above the bench (9.4 g polystyrene + 23.9 g agar). Friction 0.4 static/0.3 dynamic. 2) Lid (free, 8.7 g): clear polystyrene, outside diameter 91.0 mm, top 1.0 mm, skirt 8.0 mm high with 0.8 mm wall, rim inner edge flared 0.4 mm; seated on the base with 0.7 mm radial clearance, skirt rim 6.0 mm and top 15.0 mm above the bench. Friction 0.8/0.7. 3) Specimen: already spread on the far (+x) quarter of the agar, the area 16 to 38 mm from the centre within 30 degrees either side of +x (a cream smear; visual only). 4) Loop (free, 2.15 g): sterile single-use polystyrene 10 uL inoculating loop, 200 mm long: handle 5.0 mm diameter for its first 44 mm above the neck, then a flat finger grip 7.0 x 2.6 mm for 56 mm; neck 1.6 mm diameter x 40 mm then 1.2 mm x 55 mm; ring 5.0 mm outside diameter, 0.8 mm thick, in the plane through the axis that contains the grip's thin direction (+/-x at the start). It stands upright, ring down, axis at (0.130,-0.200), its shoulder (handle-to-neck step) on the rack's lower tier at z=0.8557; tip 8 mm above the bench. The neck's bending is lumped into one hinge 60 mm from the tip about the axis normal to the ring plane: 0.015 N m/rad (3EI/L for a 1.2 mm polystyrene neck, E=3 GPa), preloaded 2 degrees against its straight stop, 20-degree bend limit, damping 0.001 N m s/rad, armature 1e-5 kg m2. Calibrate a real loop by clamping its handle level and hanging 1.5 g on the ring: the tip drops about 3.5 mm. Friction handle 1.0/0.8, ring 0.10/0.08 (wet agar). 5) Loop rack (fixed): clear acrylic, base at (0.130,-0.200,0.7475): a 10 x 30 mm post 148 mm tall whose front face is 15 mm behind (-x) the loop axis; two 4 mm tiers glued to it, tops at 108 and 148 mm, each two 30 x 8 mm tines forming a slot open toward +x (lower 3.0 mm wide for the neck, upper 6.4 mm for the round handle), each slot's closed end 0.3 mm behind the loop. 6) Discard tray (fixed): red polypropylene autoclavable tray, 100 x 230 x 30 mm outside, 2.5 mm walls and floor, centre (0.275,-0.150,0.7475). Streak lines appear as 2.2 mm cream dots on the agar wherever the tip has ridden on it (visual readout of the scored trace; the scorer never reads it). Object jitter 0; no seeded or hidden state.
scoring: Trace: every 50 ms step, the tip (lowest point of the ring) is recorded in the plate's frame when it rests on the agar: the neck is bent at least 1.0 degree (tip pushed back >=1 mm, about 0.02 N), the tip is within 2 mm of the agar surface, and >=2 mm inside the wall. Consecutive recorded steps form one unbroken line (a touch); a hovering tip records nothing. Quadrants: the two diagonals through the plate centre at 45 degrees either side of the specimen's direction split the plate into quadrant 1 (specimen) and quadrants 2, 3, 4 going round in either direction, set by the side the first line leaving quadrant 1 goes to. A point is clearly in a quadrant when >=3 mm from both diagonals. Quadrant k (2, 3, 4) counts as streaked when all hold: (a) the touch that first goes clearly into it has, earlier in the same touch, picked up material: for quadrant 2 any point inside the specimen area; for 3 and 4 it passes within 1 mm of (crosses) a line lying in the previous quadrant drawn earlier (in an earlier touch, or >=10 mm earlier along the same touch); (b) its lines clearly inside it total >=50 mm and make >=3 back-and-forth strokes, each running >=8 mm across the quadrant; (c) from its start until the next quadrant starts, nothing is drawn clearly in a quadrant two or more back (3 stays out of 1; 4 stays out of 1 and 2); (d) the quadrants before it count. Each counted quadrant earns 0.2 (0.2, 0.4, 0.6). +0.2 plate closed, when >=1 quadrant counts: lid seated on the base (lid centre within 2.5 mm of the base centre, rim within 2 mm of its seated height, tilt within 3 degrees of the base), both grippers' centre points >=30 mm from the lid's bounding box for 1 s, and lid and base moved <1 mm and <1 degree over that second. +0.2 loop discarded, when >=1 quadrant counts: the loop's whole bounding box inside the tray's inner walls and below 10 mm above its rim, >=5 mm clear of the plate's and lid's boxes, both grippers >=30 mm from it for 1 s, and the loop moved <1 mm and <1 degree over that second (neck <0.5 rad/s). 1.0 = three quadrants + plate closed + loop discarded; success needs 1.0 held one more second. Sticky 0 for the rest of the episode, even if later undone: a gouge (tip on the agar with the neck bent >=18 degrees, a tip load of about 0.15 N, or the tip >2 mm below the agar surface); the lid touching the bench (lowest point within 2 mm of the bench while not seated); the lid taken off the plate (its centre >80 mm horizontally from the base centre); the plate tipped >15 degrees. Doing nothing scores 0; partial credit is the current end state of the plate and items. Real trial: use a mock specimen (blue food dye in 10% glycerol) or a BSL-1 strain incubated overnight; photograph the plate from above through a transparent overlay of the two diagonals with 3 mm bands and measure line lengths and strokes with a ruler; a video gives the order of quadrants, the lid's path and the 1 s stillness. Any tear, cut or furrow in the agar is a gouge.
reset_notes: New poured blood agar plate (23 mL) with the mock specimen on the far quarter, lid on, at the marked spot; a new sterile loop upright in the rack; tray emptied into autoclave waste. Reset clears the recorded trace, timers and sticky flags. Object jitter 0.
fidelity: Agar is rigid: tip contact is read from the loop neck's bend (the flexible neck lumped into one sprung hinge) plus tip height, and the streak lines are a visual readout of that contact. The ring is a solid 5 mm disc. The specimen is a printed patch and no colonies grow: isolation is judged by streak geometry. A gouge is a tip-load threshold, not a tear. Dish walls are 128-sided; rim roundings are 0.4 mm chamfers. Lid and loop masses are real (9 g, 2 g).
